events.event_name: Art Is Alive Festival — 10th Anniversary Block Party
events.what_it_is: The finale of Asase Yaa Cultural Arts Foundation's free 10th annual Art Is Alive Festival, with live performances, a street marketplace, food vendors and community programming celebrating African and African diasporic arts.
events.what_is_free: The block party and festival programming are free and open to the public; food and vendor purchases are separate.
events.caveats: The festival's individual classes can have limited capacity/reservation requirements, but the Saturday finale block party is advertised as a free public community event. This listing is specifically for the Sept. 19 block party rather than a blanket admission claim for every festival class.
events.practical_notes: Saturday Sept. 19, noon–7 PM at/around Asase Yaa School of the Arts, 506 Macdonough Street. Official Asase Yaa sources confirm the festival is free; current coverage confirms the finale block party runs noon–7 PM.

events.event_name: Return of the Buffalo: Tatanka Owe Akupi — Brooklyn Procession
events.brand: St. Ann's Warehouse × The Walk Productions × KBH Arts
events.address: Abolitionist Place to Brooklyn Bridge Park, Brooklyn, NY
events.what_it_is: A moving outdoor public-art procession of life-size buffalo puppets with music, poetry, ceremony and performances, traveling through Downtown Brooklyn from Abolitionist Place to Brooklyn Bridge Park.
events.what_is_free: The Sept. 19 Brooklyn procession is free and non-ticketed; spectators can watch or join along the public route.
events.caveats: This is a moving outdoor procession, not a seated event at St. Ann's Warehouse. The route runs from Abolitionist Place to Brooklyn Bridge Park, so there is no single fixed viewing point.
events.practical_notes: Saturday Sept. 19, 2–4:30 PM. DUMBO's current event listing confirms the Brooklyn procession route and hours; St. Ann's Warehouse is the official organizer source.

events.event_name: Slow Summer Reading Party presented by Spotify
events.brand: Reading Rhythms × Brooklyn Bridge Park × Spotify
events.address: Pier 6 Liberty Lawn, Brooklyn Bridge Park, Brooklyn, NY 11201
events.what_it_is: The final Slow Summer outdoor reading party at Brooklyn Bridge Park, with an hour of communal reading to live music, conversation and a featured-author discussion.
events.what_is_free: The reading party is free. Current event coverage also advertises giveaways for the first 300 guests.
events.caveats: Brooklyn Bridge Park lists registration for this free event. Bring your own book and blanket/towel/yoga mat; chairs are not permitted on the lawn. Normal outdoor-event capacity and weather conditions apply.
events.practical_notes: Sunday Sept. 20. Lawn opens around 12:30 PM; official Brooklyn Bridge Park programming is 1–3 PM at Pier 6 Liberty Lawn. Reading Rhythms currently lists the event as free and provides a Get Tickets/registration path.
